articles.title: Purely inseparable extensions of prime degree
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $K$ be a field of
characteristic $p$, and let $L/K$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension of degree
$[L : K] = p$. Then there are $\alpha \in L$ and $a \in K$ such that the minimal polynomial of
$\alpha$ over $K$ is $X^p - a$, $a$ is not a $p$-th power in $K$ (that is, $b^p \neq a$ for every
$b \in K$), and $L = K(\alpha)$.

articles.title: Field generated by the image of a finite algebra is finite-dimensional
articles.statement:
If `S` is finite over `R` and `χ' : S →+* K` sends `R` into the image of
`E` in `K`, then the field generated over `E` by the range of `χ'` is
finite-dimensional over `E`.

articles.title: Finite separable extensions are quotients by separable irreducible polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$
be a finite field extension. Then $L/K$ is separable if and only if there is a monic, irreducible,
separable polynomial $f \in K[X]$ such that $L$ is isomorphic as a $K$-algebra to $K[X]/(f)$.

articles.title: Integrality via the coefficients of the minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be an integrally
closed domain with fraction field $K$, and let $L$ be a field extension of $K$ that is also an
$R$-algebra, with the $R$-algebra structure on $L$ the composite of $R \to K$ and $K \to L$.
An element $x \in L$ that is algebraic over $K$ is integral over $R$ if and only if every
coefficient of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $K$ lies in the image of $R$ in $K$.

articles.title: Integrality via a lift of the minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be an integrally closed domain
with fraction field $K$, and let $L$ be a field extension of $K$ that is also an $R$-algebra,
with the $R$-algebra structure on $L$ the composite of $R \to K$ and $K \to L$. An element
$x \in L$ that is algebraic over $K$ is integral over $R$ if and only if the minimal polynomial
of $x$ over $K$ is the image of a polynomial in $R[X]$ under the map $R[X] \to K[X]$ that
applies $R \to K$ to each coefficient.

articles.title: Integrality via equality of minimal polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integrally closed domain
with fraction field $K$, and let $L$ be a field extension of $K$ that is also an $A$-algebra,
with the $A$-algebra structure on $L$ the composite of $A \to K$ and $K \to L$. An element
$\alpha \in L$ that is integral over $K$ is integral over $A$ if and only if the minimal
polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$ equals the image of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $A$
under the map $A[X] \to K[X]$ that applies $A \to K$ to each coefficient. Here the minimal
polynomial of $\alpha$ over $A$ is taken to be $0$ when $\alpha$ is not integral over $A$.

## Sources

- Proposition 1.28, in equality form.

articles.title: Algebraic closedness of rational Hahn series
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of
characteristic zero. Then the field of Hahn series over $K$ with exponents in $\mathbb{Q}$ (formal
sums $\sum_r a_r t^r$ with $a_r \in K$ whose support $\{r \in \mathbb{Q} : a_r \neq 0\}$ is
well-ordered) is algebraically closed.

articles.title: Puiseux's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let
$K((t))$ be the field of formal Laurent series over $K$, and let $K((t^{\mathbb{Q}}))$ be the field
of Hahn series over $K$ with exponents in $\mathbb{Q}$ (formal sums $\sum_r a_r t^r$ with
$a_r \in K$ whose support $\{r \in \mathbb{Q} : a_r \neq 0\}$ is well-ordered). Then:
(i) $K((t^{\mathbb{Q}}))$ is algebraically closed;
(ii) there are an injective ring homomorphism $\iota : K((t)) \to K((t^{\mathbb{Q}}))$, a subfield
$P$ of $K((t^{\mathbb{Q}}))$ containing $\iota(K((t)))$, and a ring isomorphism $e$ from $P$ onto
the algebraic closure $\overline{K((t))}$ of $K((t))$, such that $P$ consists exactly of the
series $y$ for which there is an integer $n > 0$ with every exponent in the support of $y$ of the
form $m/n$ with $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ (the Puiseux series), and $e(\iota(y))$ is the image of $y$
under the canonical embedding $K((t)) \to \overline{K((t))}$ for every $y \in K((t))$;
(iii) $K((t))$ is isomorphic as a ring to the field of fractions of the power series ring
$K[[t]]$.

Proof: Newton polygon plus Hensel lifting, first in the rational Hahn field and
then with the ramification bounded inside a power-series level.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puiseux_series

articles.title: Irreducible polynomials are expansions of separable irreducibles
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field
of characteristic $p$ (with $p = 0$ in characteristic zero) and let $f \in K[x]$ be irreducible.
Then there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and an irreducible separable polynomial $g \in K[x]$ such
that $f(x) = g(x^{p^n})$, where $0^0 = 1$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 4.5 (existence).

articles.title: Irreducible polynomials are uniquely expansions of separable irreducibles
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a
field of characteristic $p$ (with $p = 0$ in characteristic zero, and $0^0 = 1$) and let
$f \in K[x]$ be irreducible. Then there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and an
irreducible separable polynomial $g \in K[x]$ with $f(x) = g(x^{p^n})$, and for every
$n' \in \mathbb{N}$ and every irreducible separable polynomial $g' \in K[x]$ with
$f(x) = g'(x^{p^{n'}})$ we have $n' = n$ and $g' = g$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 4.5.

articles.title: The separable irreducible underlying an irreducible polynomial is unique
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a
field of characteristic $p$ (with $p = 0$ in characteristic zero) and let $f \in K[x]$ be
irreducible. If $n_1, n_2 \in \mathbb{N}$ and irreducible separable polynomials
$g_1, g_2 \in K[x]$ satisfy $f(x) = g_1(x^{p^{n_1}})$ and $f(x) = g_2(x^{p^{n_2}})$, where
$0^0 = 1$, then $n_1 = n_2$ and $g_1 = g_2$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 4.5 (uniqueness).

articles.title: Number of embeddings into a separably closed field
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable
field extension and let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra. Then the
number of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$ equals the degree $[L : K]$.

articles.title: Dedekind independence of embeddings
articles.statement:
Let $K$, $L$ and $\Omega$ be fields such that $L$
and $\Omega$ are $K$-algebras. Then the $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$, viewed as
functions $L \to \Omega$, are linearly independent over $\Omega$.

This is an instance of Dedekind's theorem on the linear independence of characters.

articles.title: Embeddings evaluated on a basis
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field extension of
degree $n$, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. Let
$b_1, \dots, b_n$ be a fixed basis of $L$ over $K$ (one particular basis chosen once and for
all, not an arbitrary one). Then the $n$ functions $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$ given
by $\varphi \mapsto \varphi(b_i)$, for $i = 1, \dots, n$, are linearly independent over
$\Omega$.

articles.title: Dimensions of the two sides of the splitting
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field
extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. Then the
base change $\Omega \otimes_K L$ and the space of functions $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$
have the same dimension as vector spaces over $\Omega$.

Both dimensions equal the degree $[L : K]$.

articles.title: The splitting isomorphism on pure tensors
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field
extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. For all
$\omega \in \Omega$ and $l \in L$, the splitting isomorphism from $\Omega \otimes_K L$ onto the
algebra $\Omega^{\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)}$ of functions $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$
sends $\omega \otimes l$ to the function $\sigma \mapsto \omega\, \sigma(l)$.

articles.title: Splitting of a separable extension over a separably closed field
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a
finite separable field extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a
$K$-algebra, and write $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms
$L \to \Omega$. The splitting isomorphism is the isomorphism of $\Omega$-algebras from
$\Omega \otimes_K L$ onto the algebra $\Omega^{\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)}$ of functions
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$ given by the evaluation homomorphism, which sends
$\omega \otimes l$ to the function $\sigma \mapsto \omega\, \sigma(l)$ and is bijective.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Proposition 4.43, field case; the book states it for finite étale $K$-algebras.

articles.title: Evaluation of embeddings at an element
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field
extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. The
evaluation map is the $K$-algebra homomorphism from $L$ to the algebra of functions
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$ sending $l \in L$ to the function
$\sigma \mapsto \sigma(l)$.

articles.title: Bijectivity of the evaluation homomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field
extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. Then the
evaluation homomorphism of $\Omega$-algebras from $\Omega \otimes_K L$ to the algebra of
functions $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$, which sends $\omega \otimes l$ to the function
$\sigma \mapsto \omega\, \sigma(l)$, is bijective.

articles.title: Injectivity of the evaluation homomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field
extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. Then the
evaluation homomorphism of $\Omega$-algebras from $\Omega \otimes_K L$ to the algebra of
functions $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$, which sends $\omega \otimes l$ to the function
$\sigma \mapsto \omega\, \sigma(l)$, is injective.

articles.title: Surjectivity of the evaluation homomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite separable field
extension, let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field that is a $K$-algebra, and write
$\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega)$ for the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$. Then the
evaluation homomorphism of $\Omega$-algebras from $\Omega \otimes_K L$ to the algebra of
functions $\mathrm{Hom}_K(L, \Omega) \to \Omega$, which sends $\omega \otimes l$ to the function
$\sigma \mapsto \omega\, \sigma(l)$, is surjective.

This follows from injectivity, since both sides have dimension $[L : K]$ over $\Omega$.

articles.title: Evaluation map on the base change to a separably closed field
articles.statement:
Let $L / K$ be a
finite separable field extension and let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field extension of
$K$. This is the homomorphism of $\Omega$-algebras from $\Omega \otimes_K L$ to the algebra
of functions from the set of $K$-algebra homomorphisms $L \to \Omega$ to $\Omega$, which
sends each pure tensor $\omega \otimes l$ to the function $\sigma \mapsto \omega \, \sigma(l)$.

articles.title: Tsen's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $k(X)$ the field of rational
functions over $k$. For all natural numbers $n$ and $d$ with $0 < d < n$, every homogeneous
polynomial $f$ of degree $d$ in $n$ variables over $k(X)$ has a nontrivial zero: there is
$x = (x_1, \dots, x_n) \in k(X)^n$ with $x_i \neq 0$ for some $i$ and $f(x) = 0$. In other
words, $k(X)$ is a $C_1$ field.

## Sources

- C. Tsen, Divisionsalgebren über Funktionenkörpern, Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 1933 335–339; reformulated by C. Chevalley and Lang; textbook in Lang, Algebra, rev 3rd ed.

articles.title: Polynomial evaluation commutes with the Frobenius power
articles.statement:
Evaluating `p` at `x ^ q` equals the `q`-th power of evaluating `p` at
`x`, where `q` is the cardinality of the finite field `F`.

articles.title: A square avoiding $0$, $1$ and $-1$ in a finite field
articles.statement:
If $F$ is a finite field with
more than five elements, then there is an element $r \in F$ with $r^2 
eq 0$, $r^2 
eq 1$
and $r^2 
eq -1$.

articles.title: Permutation polynomials $\sum_{n=1}^k n^t X^n$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an
odd prime and let $k$ and $t$ be positive integers with $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$.
Suppose that $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ or that $p - 1$ does not divide $t$. Then the map
$c \mapsto \sum_{n=1}^{k} n^t c^n$ is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ to itself.

Ding and Zieve quote this result from an earlier paper.

## Sources

- Zhiguo Ding and Michael E. Zieve, "Permutation Polynomials of the Form `∑_{n=1}^k h(n) X^n`", Theorem 1.

articles.title: When $\sum_{n=1}^k h(n) X^n$ induces the identity on $\mathbb{F}_q$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime, $\ell \ge 1$ and $q = p^\ell > 2$, and let $K$ be a finite field of characteristic
$p$ with $q$ elements. Let $k$ be a positive integer with $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(q-1)}$ and
let $h \in K[X]$, with degree $d$ (taken to be $0$ when $h = 0$) and coefficient $h_i$ of
$X^i$. Then $\sum_{n=1}^{k} h(n)\,c^n = c$ for every $c \in K$ if and only if $h(1) = 1$
and either $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ or $\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor d/(p-1) \rfloor} h_{j(p-1)} = 0$.

## Sources

- Zhiguo Ding and Michael E. Zieve, "Permutation Polynomials of the Form `∑_{n=1}^k h(n) X^n`", Theorem 2.

articles.title: Hermite–Dickson criterion
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and
characteristic $p$, and let $f \in \mathbb{F}_q[X]$. Then $f$ is a permutation polynomial of
$\mathbb{F}_q$, that is, $x \mapsto f(x)$ is a bijection of $\mathbb{F}_q$, if and only if $f$
has exactly one root in $\mathbb{F}_q$ and, for every integer $t$ with $1 \le t \le q - 2$ and
$p \nmid t$, the remainder of $f^t$ upon division by $X^q - X$ has degree at most $q - 2$.

## Sources

- Brian G. Kronenthal, "An Integer Sequence Motivated by Generalized Quadrangles", Journal of Integer Sequences 18 (2015), Article 15.7.8, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL18/Kronenthal/kron3.tex, Hermite–Dickson statement at lines 120–126.

articles.title: Power-sum criterion for distinct elements of a finite field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field
with $q$ elements and let $a_1, \dots, a_q \in K$. Then $a_1, \dots, a_q$ are pairwise distinct
if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^{q} a_i^t = 0$ for every $t = 0, 1, \dots, q - 2$ and
$\sum_{i=1}^{q} a_i^{q-1} = -1$, where $0^0 = 1$.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Unfolded form of $k$-completeness
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a
natural number. Then $f$ is complete to level $k$ if and only if for every natural number
$i \le k$ the map $F \to F$, $x \mapsto (f + iX)(x)$, is bijective, where $i$ is viewed as an
element of $F$.

articles.title: Completeness at a lower level
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and let $j \le k$
be natural numbers. If $f$ is complete to level $k$, then $f$ is complete to level $j$.

articles.title: A $k$-complete polynomial is a permutation polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field,
$f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural number. If $f$ is complete to level $k$, then $f$ is a
permutation polynomial.

articles.title: Completeness at the next level
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural
number. Then $f$ is complete to level $k + 1$ if and only if $f$ is complete to level $k$ and
$f + (k + 1)X$ is a permutation polynomial, where $k + 1$ is viewed as an element of $F$.

articles.title: Completeness at level zero
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field and $f \in F[X]$. Then $f$ is
complete to level $0$ if and only if $f$ is a permutation polynomial.

articles.title: Polynomial complete to level $k$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field,
$f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural number. The polynomial $f$ is complete to level $k$ ($k$-complete)
when $f + iX$ is a permutation polynomial for every natural number $i \le k$, where $i$ is viewed
as an element of $F$.

The source considers only positive levels $k$; here every natural level is allowed, and
completeness to level $0$ says that $f$ itself is a permutation polynomial.

articles.title: Dilated power-sum permutation polynomials of a prime field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and
let $k, t, a$ be positive integers with $p \nmid a$, $\gcd(a, p - 1) = 1$ and
$k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$. Suppose that $p - 1 \nmid t$ or $p^2 \mid k - 1$. Then the
polynomial $\sum_{n=1}^{k} (an)^t X^{an}$, with coefficients reduced modulo $p$, is a
permutation polynomial of $\mathbb{F}_p$.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Corollary 3.

articles.title: Shifted power-sum permutation polynomials of a prime field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and
let $k, t, a$ be positive integers with $\gcd(a + 1, p - 1) = 1$ and $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$.
Suppose that $p - 1 \nmid t$ or $p^2 \mid k - 1$. Then the polynomial
$\sum_{n=1}^{k} n^t X^{n+a}$, with coefficients reduced modulo $p$, is a permutation polynomial
of $\mathbb{F}_p$.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Monomial permutation polynomials of a finite field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field with $q$
elements and let $d \ge 1$ be an integer. Then $X^d$ is a permutation polynomial of $K$ if and
only if $\gcd(d, q - 1) = 1$.

The hypothesis $d \ge 1$ is needed: for $d = 0$ and $q = 2$ the condition $\gcd(d, q - 1) = 1$
holds, but $X^0 = 1$ is constant.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Permutation polynomial over a finite field
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f$ over a finite field $F$ is a
permutation polynomial when its evaluation map $F \to F$, $x \mapsto f(x)$, is bijective.

articles.title: Rational form of the power-weighted geometric sum
articles.statement:
For positive integers $t$ and $k$,
the following identity holds in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$:

$$(1 - X)^{t+1} \sum_{n=1}^{k} n^t X^n =
\sum_{n=1}^{t} \Bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (-1)^i \binom{t+1}{i} (n - i)^t\Bigr) X^n +
\sum_{m=1}^{t+1} \Bigl(\sum_{i=m}^{t+1} (-1)^i \binom{t+1}{i} (k + m - i)^t\Bigr) X^{k+m}.$$

Equivalently, for every $x \ne 1$ the value $h_t^k(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{k} n^t x^n$ is the
right-hand side at $x$ divided by $(1 - x)^{t+1}$, which is the form the source states.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Lemma 4.

articles.title: Vishwakarma–Singh congruence for ordered partitions into multiples
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd
prime and let $a, k, s, t$ be positive integers with $\gcd(a, p - 1) = 1$, $s \le p - 2$ and
$k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$, such that $p^2 \mid k - 1$ whenever $p - 1 \mid t$. Let
$\mu = \lfloor aks/(p - 1) \rfloor$. Then

$$\sum_{j=1}^{\mu} \sum_{\omega} (\omega_1 \cdots \omega_s)^t \equiv 0 \pmod{p},$$

where for each $j$ the inner sum runs over all $s$-tuples $\omega = (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_s)$
with entries in $\{an : 1 \le n \le k\}$ and $\omega_1 + \cdots + \omega_s = j(p - 1)$.

The source states this with two differences. It assumes $s \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ in place of
$s \le p - 2$; with that hypothesis the claim fails, e.g. for $a = 1$, $p = 3$, $k = 7$, $s = 2$,
$t = 1$. It takes $\mu = \lfloor ks/(p - 1) \rfloor$; with that bound the claim fails for $a > 1$,
e.g. for $p = 5$, $a = 3$, $k = 21$, $s = t = 1$ the sum is $12$. The bound
$\lfloor aks/(p - 1) \rfloor$ covers every multiple of $p - 1$ up to $aks$, the degree of the
$s$-th power of $\sum_{n=1}^{k} (an)^t X^{an}$, to which the proof applies Hermite's criterion.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Vishwakarma–Singh congruence for ordered partitions
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let
$k, s, t$ be positive integers with $s \le p - 2$ and $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$, such that
$p^2 \mid k - 1$ whenever $p - 1 \mid t$. Let $\mu = \lfloor ks/(p - 1) \rfloor$. Then

$$\sum_{j=1}^{\mu} \sum_{\omega} (\omega_1 \cdots \omega_s)^t \equiv 0 \pmod{p},$$

where for each $j$ the inner sum runs over all $s$-tuples $\omega = (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_s)$
with entries in $\{1, \dots, k\}$ and $\omega_1 + \cdots + \omega_s = j(p - 1)$.

The source states the hypothesis $s \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ in place of $s \le p - 2$, the range
of Hermite's criterion used in its proof; with that hypothesis the claim fails, e.g. for $p = 3$,
$k = 1$, $s = 2$, $t = 1$ the sum is $1$.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Vishwakarma–Singh congruence for ordered partitions, linear case
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd
prime and let $k, s$ be positive integers with $s \le p - 2$ and $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$.
Let $\mu = \lfloor ks/(p - 1) \rfloor$. Then

$$\sum_{j=1}^{\mu} \sum_{\omega} \omega_1 \cdots \omega_s \equiv 0 \pmod{p},$$

where for each $j$ the inner sum runs over all $s$-tuples $\omega = (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_s)$
with entries in $\{1, \dots, k\}$ and $\omega_1 + \cdots + \omega_s = j(p - 1)$.

This is the case $t = 1$ of the source's Theorem 1. The source states the hypothesis
$s \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ in place of $s \le p - 2$; with that hypothesis the claim fails, e.g.
for $p = 3$, $k = 7$, $s = 2$ the sum is $400 \equiv 1 \pmod{3}$.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Alternating binomial sums of powers
articles.statement:
Let $x, y, k \in \mathbb{C}$ and let $n, m$ be
positive integers. If $n = m$, then

$$\sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \binom{n}{i} (kx + iy)^m = (-1)^n y^n n!,$$

and if $m < n$, then $\sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \binom{n}{i} (kx + iy)^m = 0$.

## Sources

- Chandan Kumar Vishwakarma and Rajesh P. Singh, *A Congruence Identity on Ordered Partitions Using Permutation Polynomials*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A12, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Power sums over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $t$ a positive
integer. Then $\sum_{a \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}} a^t$ equals $-1$ if $p - 1$ divides $t$,
and $0$ otherwise.

## Sources

- Zhiguo Ding and Michael E. Zieve, "Permutation Polynomials of the Form `∑_{n=1}^k h(n) X^n`", Lemma 1.

articles.title: Primitive polynomials via primitive roots of unity
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $f \in F[X]$, and let $n$ be the degree of $f$ (with $n = 0$ if $f = 0$). Let
$\alpha$ be the class of $X$ in the quotient ring $F[X]/(f)$. Then $f$ is primitive if and only
if $f$ is monic, $f$ is irreducible, and $\alpha$ is a primitive $(q^n - 1)$-th root of unity,
that is, $\alpha^{q^n - 1} = 1$ and $q^n - 1$ divides every natural number $l$ with
$\alpha^l = 1$.

articles.title: Defining characterization of primitive polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $f \in F[X]$, and let $n$ be the degree of $f$ (with $n = 0$ if $f = 0$). Then $f$
is primitive if and only if $f$ is monic, $f$ is irreducible, and the class of $X$ in the
quotient ring $F[X]/(f)$ has multiplicative order $q^n - 1$.

articles.title: Primitive polynomials are irreducible
articles.statement:
Every primitive polynomial over a finite field is
irreducible.

articles.title: Primitive polynomial over a finite field
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements,
let $f \in F[X]$, and let $n$ be the degree of $f$ (with $n = 0$ if $f = 0$). Then $f$ is
primitive if it is monic, it is irreducible, and the class of $X$ in the quotient ring
$F[X]/(f)$ has multiplicative order $q^n - 1$.

articles.title: Primitive polynomials are monic
articles.statement:
Every primitive polynomial over a finite field is
monic.

articles.title: Order of the root of a primitive polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements
and let $f \in F[X]$ be a primitive polynomial of degree $n$. Then the class of $X$ in the
quotient ring $F[X]/(f)$ has multiplicative order $q^n - 1$.

articles.title: Primitive polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $f$ be a
polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and let $n$ be the degree of $f$ (with $n = 0$ if
$f = 0$). Then $f$ is primitive if and only if $f$ is monic, $f$ is irreducible, and the class of
$X$ in the quotient ring $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})[X]/(f)$ has multiplicative order $p^n - 1$.

## Sources

- ATLAS Definition 3.14.

articles.title: Monic irreducible binary polynomials exist in every degree
articles.statement: Over `ZMod 2`, there is a monic irreducible polynomial of every positive degree.

articles.title: Minimality of the binary modulus found by exhaustive search
articles.statement:
The returned modulus is no larger than any lower coefficient word whose monic modulus is
irreducible.

articles.title: Exhaustive search returns an irreducible binary modulus
articles.statement: At every positive width, exhaustive search returns an irreducible binary modulus.

articles.title: Exhaustive search for an irreducible binary modulus
articles.statement:
Search the lower coefficient words in ascending order for the first word passing the
exhaustive inverse test. Width zero is deliberately reported as failure.

articles.title: Inverse test succeeds exactly for irreducible moduli
articles.statement:
At positive width, the exhaustive inverse test succeeds exactly for irreducible monic
moduli.

articles.title: Exhaustive inverse test for a binary polynomial modulus
articles.statement:
Test exhaustively whether every nonzero word has a multiplicative inverse modulo
`g.monicModulus`.

articles.title: Additive Hilbert 90, pointwise form
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite-dimensional Galois extension
and let $\sigma$ be a $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ that generates its Galois group, that is,
every $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ is an integer power of $\sigma$. If $x \in L$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(x) = 0$, then there is $y \in L$ with $\sigma(y) - y = x$.

articles.title: Additive Hilbert 90 for cyclic extensions
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite-dimensional Galois
extension and let $\sigma$ be a $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ that generates its Galois group,
that is, every $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ is an integer power of $\sigma$. Then the kernel
of the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K} \colon L \to K$ equals the image of the $K$-linear map
$\sigma - 1 \colon L \to L$, $y \mapsto \sigma(y) - y$.

articles.title: Norm in a tensor product with a Galois extension
articles.statement:
For a Galois extension `M / F` and any `F`-algebra `R`, the norm of an
element of `R ⊗[F] M` over `R` is the product of its Galois conjugates.

articles.title: The roots generate the function field
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the intermediate
field of $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by the roots
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ is the whole function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

articles.title: Elementary symmetric polynomials evaluated at the roots
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$
and $k$, the image of the $k$-th elementary symmetric polynomial
$e_k \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the
$k$-th elementary symmetric function of the multiset of roots $\{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$, that is,
the sum of the products $x_{i_1} \cdots x_{i_k}$ over all $i_1 < \dots < i_k$.

articles.title: Polynomials in the roots
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and every polynomial
$p \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$, the image of $p$ in the function field
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ lies in the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra generated by the roots
$x_1, \dots, x_n$.

articles.title: The coefficients are algebraically independent
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the
coefficients $a_1, \dots, a_n$ of the general polynomial, the elementary symmetric functions of
$x_1, \dots, x_n$, are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the function field
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

articles.title: Algebraic independence of the elementary symmetric polynomials
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n$, the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_1, \dots, e_n \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ are
algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

This follows from the fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials.

articles.title: Injective algebra maps preserve algebraic independence
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative
$\mathbb{C}$-algebras, let $f : A \to B$ be an injective $\mathbb{C}$-algebra homomorphism, and
let $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $A$ that is algebraically independent over
$\mathbb{C}$. Then the family $(f(x_i))_{i \in \iota}$ is algebraically independent over
$\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: The roots are algebraically independent
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the roots
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the function field
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

articles.title: Upper bound for the essential dimension of symmetric groups
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\operatorname{ed}(S_n) \le n - 3$ for every natural number $n \ge 5$.

## Sources

- Buhler--Reichstein (1997), the classical Tschirnhaus bound `ed_ℂ(Sₙ) ≤ n - 3` for `n ≥ 5`.

articles.title: Lower bound for the essential dimension of symmetric groups
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor \le \operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for every natural number $n$.

## Sources

- Buhler--Reichstein (1997) and Duncan, the lower bound `⌊n/2⌋ ≤ ed_ℂ(Sₙ)`.

articles.title: Coefficients in the coefficient field
articles.statement:
For $0 \le i < n$, the coefficient $a_{i+1}$,
the $(i+1)$-st elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, regarded as an element of the
coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$.

articles.title: Coefficients indexed by degree
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, for $1 \le k \le n$ let $a_k$
be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$ in the function field
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, and let $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ be the coefficient field. For
each natural number $k$, the element $c_k$ of $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is defined by
$c_0 = 1$, $c_k = a_k$ for $1 \le k \le n$, and $c_k = 0$ for $k > n$.

In a variable $X$, the general polynomial is $\sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k c_k X^{n-k}$.

articles.title: The coefficients of the general polynomial
articles.statement:
For $0 \le i < n$, the coefficient
$a_{i+1}$ is the $(i+1)$-st elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, as an element of
the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

articles.title: Essential dimension of the symmetric group on five letters
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\operatorname{ed}(S_5) = 2$.

## Sources

- Buhler--Reichstein (1997), exact value `ed_ℂ(S₅) = 2`: their general bounds `⌊5/2⌋ ≤ ed_ℂ(S₅) ≤ 5 - 3` coincide at `2`. The classical Bring--Jerrard form `X^5 + pX + q` is not the descent behind that upper bound here: producing it already requires solving auxiliary equations over an extension of the coefficient field, and normalizing further to `X^5 + X + a` is again only a scaling over an extension, so neither form witnesses a descent over the original field in the sense of this file (in particular nothing here implies `edSn 5 ≤ 1`).

articles.title: Essential dimension of the symmetric group on four letters
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\operatorname{ed}(S_4) = 2$.

## Sources

- Buhler--Reichstein (1997), exact value `ed_ℂ(S₄) = 2`.

articles.title: Trivial upper bound for the essential dimension of $S_n$
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $n$, the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, in the
general-polynomial parameter sense, is at most $n$.

The bound comes from the trivial descent, whose parameter field is the coefficient field of
the general polynomial, of transcendence degree $n$.

articles.title: Essential dimension of the symmetric group on seven letters
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\operatorname{ed}(S_7) = 4$.

## Sources

- Duncan (2010), *Essential dimensions of `A₇` and `S₇`*, exact value `ed_ℂ(S₇) = 4`. Buhler--Reichstein's general bounds give only `3 ≤ ed_ℂ(S₇) ≤ 4` here.

articles.title: Essential dimension of the symmetric group on six letters
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\operatorname{ed}(S_6) = 3$.

## Sources

- Buhler--Reichstein (1997), exact value `ed_ℂ(S₆) = 3`.

articles.title: Essential dimension of the symmetric group
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be the field of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates. The
essential dimension of $S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, in the general-polynomial parameter sense, is
the least natural number $d$ such that some intermediate field $F_0$ of
$\mathbb{C} \subseteq \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of transcendence degree at most $d$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ admits an intermediate field $E_0$ for which $(F_0, E_0)$ is a descent of the
general polynomial extension.

The transcendence degree is read as a natural number (an infinite degree would count as $0$;
this does not occur, since $F_0$ lies in the coefficient field).

articles.title: The essential-dimension ratio of the symmetric groups is at most one
articles.statement:
The constant
$C_{79}$, the limit superior as $n \to \infty$ of $\operatorname{ed}_{\mathbb{C}}(S_n) / n$ with
the essential dimension of $S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$ taken in the general-polynomial parameter
sense, satisfies $C_{79} \le 1$.

articles.title: Lower bound for the asymptotic essential-dimension ratio
articles.statement:
Write
$\operatorname{ed}(S_n)$ for the essential dimension of the symmetric group $S_n$ over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial sense: the least transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$
of a subfield $F_0$ of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general
polynomial of degree $n$ over which that polynomial descends up to Tschirnhaus transformation.
Then $\limsup_{n \to \infty} \operatorname{ed}(S_n)/n \ge 1/2$.

## Sources

- catalogue lower row for `C₇₉`, from the `⌊n/2⌋` lower bound: `1/2 ≤ C₇₉`.

articles.title: Asymptotic essential-dimension ratio of the symmetric groups
articles.statement:
The catalogue constant
$C_{79}$ is the limit superior, as $n \to \infty$, of $\operatorname{ed}_{\mathbb{C}}(S_n) / n$,
where $\operatorname{ed}_{\mathbb{C}}(S_n)$ is the essential dimension of the symmetric group
$S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$ in the general-polynomial parameter sense.

articles.title: Coefficient field of the general polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be the field of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates and,
for $1 \le k \le n$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of
$x_1, \dots, x_n$. The coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is the intermediate
field of $\mathbb{C} \subseteq \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by
$a_1, \dots, a_n$.

articles.title: General polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be the
indeterminates of the rational function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, let $a_0 = 1$ and,
for $1 \le k \le n$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of
$x_1, \dots, x_n$. The general polynomial of degree $n$ is the polynomial
$\sum_{j=0}^{n} (-1)^j a_j X^{n-j} = X^n - a_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n a_n$ with
coefficients in the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$.

articles.title: Rational functions are algebraic over the polynomial subalgebra
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$n$, every element of the field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of rational functions in $n$
indeterminates is algebraic over the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra generated by $x_1, \dots, x_n$:
it is a ratio of two polynomials in $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

articles.title: Distinct linear factors are coprime
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and distinct elements
$a \ne b$ of the field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of rational functions in $n$
indeterminates, the polynomials $X - a$ and $X - b$ are coprime in
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)[X]$: there are polynomials $u$ and $v$ with
$u (X - a) + v (X - b) = 1$.

articles.title: The trivial descent
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the pair $(F, E)$ is a descent of
the general polynomial extension, where $E = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the field of
rational functions in $n$ indeterminates and $F = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is the
coefficient field, generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by the elementary symmetric functions
$a_1, \dots, a_n$ of $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

The general polynomial serves as the defining polynomial of this descent.

articles.title: Descent of the general polynomial extension
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$E = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be the field of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates and
let $F = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n) \subseteq E$ be the coefficient field of the general
polynomial, where $a_k$ is the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$. A
pair $(F_0, E_0)$ of intermediate fields of $\mathbb{C} \subseteq E$ is a descent when
$F_0 \subseteq F$, $F_0 \subseteq E_0$, $E_0 \cap F = F_0$, the compositum of $E_0$ and $F$ is
all of $E$, and there is a nonzero polynomial $p$ with coefficients in $F_0$ whose image in
$E[X]$ splits and is separable, such that $E_0$ is the field generated over $F_0$ by the
roots of $p$ in $E$.

Splitting and separability are imposed in $E$, where they say that the roots of $p$ are all
present and distinct.

articles.title: The roots of the general polynomial generate the function field
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
let $E_n = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function
of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, let $F_n = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n) \subseteq E_n$ be the coefficient
field, and let $f_n = X^n - a_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n a_n \in F_n[X]$ be the general
polynomial. The subfield of $E_n$ generated over $F_n$ by all roots of $f_n$ in $E_n$ is $E_n$
itself.

articles.title: The roots $x_i$ are pairwise distinct
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the elements
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ of the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ are pairwise distinct:
$x_i = x_j$ implies $i = j$.

articles.title: Each $x_i$ is a root of the general polynomial
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$E_n = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of
$x_1, \dots, x_n$, and let $f_n = X^n - a_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n a_n$ be the general
polynomial, with coefficients in $F_n = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n) \subseteq E_n$. Then
$f_n(x_i) = 0$ in $E_n$ for every $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$.

articles.title: The roots $x_i$
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$, $x_i$ is the $i$-th
indeterminate of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, viewed as an element of its
fraction field, the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

These elements are the roots of the general polynomial.

articles.title: The function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the function
field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the fraction field of the polynomial ring
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ indeterminates.

articles.title: The product of the linear factors $X - x_i$ is separable
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
the polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n} (X - x_i)$ over the function field
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is separable.

articles.title: Transcendence degree of the coefficient field
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $a_k$ be the
$k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$ in $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$. The
coefficient field $F_n = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of the general polynomial has numeric
transcendence degree $n$ over $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Numeric transcendence degree
articles.statement:
For a field $F$ that is a $\mathbb{C}$-algebra, the numeric
transcendence degree of $F$ is its transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$ as a natural number when
that degree is finite, and $0$ when it is infinite.

articles.title: Transcendence degree of $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ has transcendence degree $n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, as a
cardinal.

articles.title: Degree of a finite extension of the reals
articles.statement:
If $E$ is a field that is a finite-dimensional
algebra over $\mathbb{R}$, then the dimension of $E$ as a real vector space is $1$ or $2$.

This follows because such a field $E$ is isomorphic as an $\mathbb{R}$-algebra to $\mathbb{R}$ or
to $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Galois groups over the reals have order 1 or 2
articles.statement:
If $E$ is a finite Galois extension of
$\mathbb{R}$, then the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{R})$ has order $1$ or $2$.

articles.title: Galois groups over the reals have order a power of 2
articles.statement:
If $E$ is a finite Galois extension
of $\mathbb{R}$, then the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{R})$ has order $2^n$ for some natural
number $n$.

In fact the order is $1$ or $2$.

## Sources

- the book's lemma in Lecture 34 (Main Theorem of Algebra).

articles.title: Gauss–Wantzel theorem
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 3$, the real number
$\cos(2\pi/n)$ is constructible (it lies in the smallest subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under
square roots) if and only if $n$ is a Gauss–Wantzel number, that is, every prime factor of $n$ is
$2$ or a Fermat prime and every odd prime factor of $n$ divides $n$ only once.

## Sources

- C. F. Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), §365-366; P. L. Wantzel, Recherches sur les moyens de reconnaître si un problème de géométrie peut se résoudre avec la règle et le compas, J. Math. Pures Appl. 1 (1837). Listed as §174 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Knill, §174. Problem `gauss_wantzel_constructible_polygon` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Gauss–Wantzel number
articles.statement:
A natural number $n$ is a Gauss–Wantzel number if $n > 0$, every
prime factor of $n$ is either $2$ or a Fermat prime, and $p^2$ does not divide $n$ for every odd
prime factor $p$ of $n$.

Equivalently, $n$ is a power of $2$ times a product of distinct Fermat primes.

articles.title: Constructible real numbers
articles.statement:
The constructible real numbers form the smallest set of real
numbers that contains every rational number and is closed under addition, negation,
multiplication, inverses of nonzero elements and square roots of nonnegative elements;
equivalently, the smallest subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under square roots.

These are the real values constructible from rational data by straightedge and compass.

articles.title: Extensions of prime degree with a nontrivial automorphism are Galois
articles.statement:
In an extension of prime degree, a nontrivial automorphism witnesses
that the extension is Galois, has order equal to the degree, and generates
the automorphism group.

articles.title: Intermediate fields of an abelian extension form a modular lattice
articles.statement:
If $L/K$ is a
finite-dimensional abelian Galois extension, then the lattice of intermediate fields of $L/K$
is modular.

The proof transports the modular lattice of subgroups of the commutative Galois group across
the Galois correspondence.

articles.title: Abel–Ruffini theorem
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Every complex root of every
polynomial with rational coefficients of degree exactly $n$ is expressible by radicals over
$\mathbb{Q}$ if and only if $n \le 4$. Here a complex number is expressible by radicals over
$\mathbb{Q}$ when it lies in the smallest subfield $S$ of $\mathbb{C}$ such that $z \in S$
whenever $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and $z^k \in S$ for some integer $k \ge 1$.

The direction from radical solvability to $n \le 4$ is the classical insolvability of the
general quintic, extended to higher degrees; the converse follows from the explicit formulas
of Cardano and Ferrari for degrees at most four.

## Sources

- P. Ruffini (1799), N. H. Abel (1824), É. Galois (1832). Listed as §57 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf); the general-quintic insolvability is #16 on Freek Wiedijk's *Formalizing 100 Theorems* list (https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/). Problem `abel_ruffini` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Abel–Ruffini, contrapositive form
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $E$ be a field extension of $F$,
and let $n \ge 5$. If $p \in F[X]$ is irreducible and the Galois group of $p$ over $F$ is isomorphic
to the symmetric group $S_n$, then no root of $p$ in $E$ is solvable by radicals over $F$.

articles.title: Abel–Ruffini for $S_5$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $E$ be a field extension of $F$. If
$p \in F[X]$ is irreducible and the Galois group of $p$ over $F$ is isomorphic to the symmetric
group $S_5$, then no root of $p$ in $E$ is solvable by radicals over $F$.

articles.title: Solvable extensions ↔ solvable groups
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero and let
$p \in F[X]$ be a nonzero polynomial. Every root of $p$ in an algebraic closure $\overline{F}$ of
$F$ is solvable by radicals over $F$ (obtainable from $F$ by field operations and $n$-th roots
inside $\overline{F}$) if and only if the Galois group of $p$ over $F$ is solvable.

## Sources

- É. Galois (1832); the iff appears in standard texts such as Stewart, *Galois Theory* (Theorem 18.10); Lang, *Algebra* (VI §7); Rotman, *Galois Theory* (Theorem 73). Listed as §58 (additional statement 2) in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `solvable_by_radicals_converse` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The closure of a Galois subgroup is the fixing group of its fixed field
articles.statement:
Let $K/k$ be a
Galois extension, not necessarily finite, and give $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ the Krull topology.
For every subgroup $H$ of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ with fixed field $K^H$, the closure of $H$
equals the subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ consisting of the automorphisms that fix $K^H$
pointwise.
